subject.title: fix(ssrf): allow loopback for hostnames in allowedHostnames list (#101965)

question: Should browser allowlisted hostnames bypass all DNS-answer checks, or should this fix only restore a loopback-specific exception while preserving metadata/link-local blocking?
rationale: Both choices change the browser SSRF trust boundary; automation cannot safely decide whether operator allowlists should authorize metadata/link-local targets or only the reported loopback alias case.

options.title: Narrow the exception before merge
options.body: Keep the browser-only owner boundary, but continue rejecting metadata/link-local DNS answers and only permit the maintainer-approved loopback case with tests.

options.title: Approve full allowlist bypass
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept that browser `allowedHostnames` and `hostnameAllowlist` entries bypass DNS-answer checks entirely, with docs and proof updated for that contract.

options.title: Pause on the canonical issue
options.body: Leave this PR blocked while the browser/SSRF contract is settled on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101965.

recommendation.title: Narrow the exception before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the browser-only owner boundary, but continue rejecting metadata/link-local DNS answers and only permit the maintainer-approved loopback case with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened the canonical issue and have recent browser SSRF policy history in the affected area.
